comparisons.peer_summary: Revenue increased $2.3 billion to $21.8 billion, primarily due to higher sales and trading revenue ($1.4 billion increase) and investment banking fees, driven by gains in Equities and FICC.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC reported revenue growth, but the drivers and magnitudes differed significantly. C's Services revenue increased 9% (3% excluding Argentina devaluation), driven largely by non-interest revenue. BAC's Global Markets revenue increased $2.3 billion to $21.8 billion, driven primarily by higher sales and trading revenue and investment banking fees, with no mention of currency devaluation impacts similar to C's Argentina exposure.

sentences.text: Services revenues of $19.6 billion increased 9%, largely driven by a 28% increase in non-interest revenue and higher net interest income (up 1%).

Excluding the impact of the Argentina currency devaluation ($(178) million in 2024 versus approximately $(1.2) billion in 2023), Services revenues increased 3% and its non-interest revenue increased 5%.
Revenue increased $2.3 billion to $21.8 billion primarily due to higher sales and trading revenue and investment banking fees.

comparisons.peer_summary: Net revenues increased 16% to $53.51 billion in 2024, driven primarily by higher revenues in Global Banking & Markets (Equities, Investment banking, FICC) and Asset & Wealth Management (Equity investments, Management fees), with slight increases in Platform Solutions.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and GS reported significant revenue growth in 2024, but the composition differed: C's Services segment growth was heavily impacted by currency devaluation in Argentina which inflated the reported rate, whereas GS's overall net revenue growth was driven by higher principal transactions, investment banking, and net interest income without mentioning adverse currency devaluations. GS reported a 16% increase in net revenues compared to C's reported 9% increase in Services revenue, though C's underlying growth excluding Argentina was 3%.
